sentences.text: The type specimen of Sachicasaurus measured approximately 10 to 10.35 meters long and weighed between 10.3 and 12.8 metric tons.
This animal is characterized by a very short lower jaw symphysis and a reduced number of lower teeth, ranging from 17 to 18 compared to 25 to 40 in other pliosaurids.
Sachicasaurus is an extinct genus of pliosaurid found in the Barremian of the Paja Formation in the Colombian Eastern Ranges of the Andes.
The holotype specimen of Sachicasaurus was discovered in 2013.
The genus name Sachicasaurus is derived from the location of the fossil find, Sáchica, and the Greek word for lizard.
The species name vitae means "of life" in Latin, chosen to reflect the vitality the discovery brought to the town of Sáchica.
Sachicasaurus is classified as a brachauchenine pliosaurid.
Sachicasaurus belongs to the family Pliosauridae.
Sachicasaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 113.2 million years ago.
Sachicasaurus shared its environment with three other pliosaurids: Acostasaurus, Stenorhynchosaurus, and Monquirasaurus.
Sachicasaurus coexisted with elasmosaurids, marine turtles, and ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs in the same region.
